sub: Named after aṭ-ṭāriq, “the night visitor”, in ayah 1
theme: Man is watched, was made from a drop, and will be raised with his secrets exposed. The Quran is decisive truth, and no plot against it will succeed.
story: Revealed in Makkah, at a time when the Quraysh were using every trick and plan to defeat the Quran and the Prophet ﷺ.
It makes two points. First, man will stand before Allah after death: the One who made him from a drop can bring him back, and on that Day every secret is exposed.
Second, the Quran is a decisive word, not a joke. The disbelievers are plotting, but Allah has His own plan, so the Prophet ﷺ is told to give them a little time.

sections.title: Made from a drop, raised again
sections.meaning: By the sky and the piercing star: every soul has a guardian over it. So let man look at what he was made from: a gushing fluid. The One who made him can bring him back, on the Day secrets are exposed and he has no strength and no helper.
points: By the sky and aṭ-ṭāriq, the piercing star
Every soul has a guardian over it
Look at your origin: a gushing fluid
He can surely bring him back
Secrets exposed; no strength, no helper
sections.matters: It takes the most common doubt, how dust could live again, and answers it with man’s own beginning. If Allah made you from a drop, bringing you back is no harder.
sections.story: Reportedly, Abū Ṭālib was eating bread and milk with the Prophet ﷺ when a star shot across the sky, and he was frightened. The Prophet ﷺ told him it was a star thrown, one of Allah’s signs, and ayah 1 was revealed.
explained: Aṭ-ṭāriq is anything that comes by night; here it is the star, an-najm ath-thāqib, whose light pierces the dark. The oath’s answer: every soul has a ḥāfiẓ over it, angels who record its deeds, or who guard it from harm by Allah’s command.

So look at your beginning: a gushing fluid from between the backbone and the ribs. The One who made you from that can easily bring you back. On that Day the sarāʾir, hidden beliefs, intentions and deeds, are tested and laid bare, and man has no strength in himself and no helper outside.
teaches: Your deeds are being recorded even when no one else sees.
Your humble beginning is proof that Allah can bring you back.
Private intentions will be exposed, so keep them clean.
On that Day, no strength or supporter can save you.
sections.hook: Question, then answer: “What is aṭ-ṭāriq?” (2) → “the piercing star” (3). Man looks back at his origin (5) and forward to his return (8). It ends: no strength, no helper (10).

sections.title: A decisive word, and their plot
sections.meaning: By the sky that returns rain and the earth that splits with plants: the Quran is a decisive word, not a joke. They plot a plot, and Allah plans too. So give the disbelievers time, just a little while.
points: By the sky that returns rain, the earth that splits
The Quran: a decisive word, not a joke
Give the disbelievers time, a little while
sections.matters: It answers the second doubt: that the Quran can be mocked or beaten. Like rain and crops, it is serious and real, and every plan against it will fail. It also tells the Prophet ﷺ to be patient.
sections.story: No specific incident. The Quraysh were plotting against the Prophet ﷺ and the Quran. The short respite of ayah 17 ended when they were defeated at Badr.
explained: A second oath: the sky dhāt ar-rajʿ, returning rain again and again, and the earth dhāt aṣ-ṣadʿ, cracking open for plants. The answer: the Quran is qawl faṣl, a word that separates truth from falsehood. It is not hazl, not a joke.

The disbelievers yakīdūna kaydā, scheming to push the truth away. Allah says: I too am planning, leading them on in ways they don’t notice, so that the truth wins. So don’t rush against them. Give them a little time; they will see the result.
teaches: Take the Quran seriously; it is not entertainment.
No plot against Allah’s truth can succeed.
Patience with opponents is part of trusting Allah’s plan.
Rain and crops are no game, and neither is the Quran’s message.
sections.hook: The surah swears by the sky twice: with the star (1) and with the earth (11). Kayd is doubled (15–16), and so is the command to give them time (17: mahhil… amhilhum).

groups.text: By the sky and the night visitor: the star whose light pierces the dark.
Every single soul has a guardian over it.
Let man look at his origin: a gushing fluid from between the backbone and ribs.
Allah can bring him back, on the Day secrets are exposed and no one can help him.
By the sky that returns rain and the earth that splits: the Quran is decisive, not a joke.
They plot and Allah plans, so give the disbelievers a little time.

1.explain: Allah swears by the sky and aṭ-ṭāriq: anything that comes at night. Stars are called this because they appear at night and hide by day.
1.why: Reportedly revealed when Abū Ṭālib, eating with the Prophet ﷺ, was startled by a shooting star. The Prophet ﷺ told him it was a star thrown, one of Allah’s signs.

2.explain: Wa mā adrāka: “and what will make you know?” The question shows how great the thing is before it is named.

3.explain: An-najm ath-thāqib: the star whose light pierces the darkness. Any bright star; some named the Pleiades or Saturn.

4.explain: Every soul has a ḥāfiẓ over it: angels recording its good and bad deeds, or angels guarding it from harms Allah has not decreed (13:11).

5.explain: So let man reflect: from what was he created? A look meant to teach a lesson, not just to see.

6.explain: From a māʾ dāfiq, a gushing fluid. The child comes from both parents, by Allah’s permission.

7.explain: It comes from between aṣ-ṣulb, the backbone, and at-tarāʾib, the ribs or chest bones: either the man’s backbone and the woman’s chest, or both in the man.

8.explain: Rajʿih: bringing him back. The One who made him from that fluid can surely raise him after death, and beginning creation is no easier than repeating it.

9.explain: Tublā as-sarāʾir: secrets are tested and exposed: hidden beliefs, intentions, and private duties like prayer and fasting that only Allah saw.

10.explain: He has no quwwah, strength within himself, and no nāṣir, helper from outside, to protect him from the punishment.

11.explain: Dhāt ar-rajʿ: the sky that returns, sending rain again and again each year. Without it, people and animals would perish.

12.explain: Dhāt aṣ-ṣadʿ: the earth that cracks open to bring out plants and trees.

13.explain: Innahu: the Quran is qawl faṣl, a decisive word that separates truth from falsehood, true and plain.

14.explain: Wa mā huwa bil-hazl: it is serious, not play or empty talk.

15.explain: They, the deniers of the Prophet ﷺ and the Quran, are scheming to push the truth away and prop up falsehood.

16.explain: And Allah plans: leading them on step by step from where they don’t realise, so the truth wins. Man is far too weak to outplan Him.

17.explain: Mahhil, amhilhum ruwaydā: give them respite, just a little. The command is repeated in two forms for emphasis. They were later seized at Badr.
